stem: A coil consists of 400 turns of wire. Each turn is a square of side \(d = 20\) cm. A uniform magnetic field directed perpendicular to the plane of the coil is turned on. If the field changes linearly from 0 to 0.50 T in 0.8 s, what is the magnitude of induced emf in the coil while the field is changing?
solution:
The magnitude of induced emf in the coil is written as

\(|e| = \left| \dfrac{\mathrm{d}(N\phi)}{\mathrm{d}t} \right| = N \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\)

\(\because \phi = B \cdot A\)

\(\therefore |e| = N \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}(BA)}{\mathrm{d}t}\)

\(= N \cdot A \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) (as \(A\) is constant and \(B\) is changing with time)

\(= N \cdot A \cdot \dfrac{\Delta B}{\Delta t} = N \cdot A \cdot \dfrac{B_{\text{final}} - B_{\text{initial}}}{\Delta t}\)

Inserting the given values of \(N = 400\), \(A = (20\ \text{cm})^2 = (0.2\ \text{m})^2\), \(B_{\text{final}} = 0.5\) T, \(B_{\text{initial}} = 0\), \(\Delta t = 0.8\) s, we find the induced emf

\(|e| = \dfrac{400 \cdot (0.20\ \text{m})^2 (0.5\ \text{T})}{0.8\ \text{s}}\)

\(= 10\) Volt

subtopic: Induced emf in a Stationary Coil
stem: A long solenoid S, as shown in the figure has 200 turns/cm and carries a current \(i\) of 1.4 A. The diameter \(D\) of the solenoid is 3 cm. A coil C, having 100 turns and diameter \(d\) of 2 cm is kept coaxial to the solenoid. The current in the solenoid is decreased steadily to zero in 20 ms. Calculate the magnitude of emf induced in the coil C when the current in the solenoid is changing.
solution:
Part of magnetic flux (per turn) of the solenoid S that links with the coil C is

\(\phi_{\text{c}} = \mu_0\, n_{\text{s}}\, i\, \dfrac{\pi\, \mathrm{d}_{\text{c}}^{2}}{4}\)

This flux reduces to zero in \(\mathrm{d}t = 20\) ms. Thus, the emf induced in coil C of \(N_{\text{c}}\) turns is

\(e_{\text{s}} = -N_{\text{c}} \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\phi_{\text{c}}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{-(0 - \phi_{\text{c}})}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mu_0 N_{\text{c}} n_{\text{s}} i \pi\, \mathrm{d}_{\text{c}}^{2}}{4\,\mathrm{d}t}\)

\(= \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100 \times 2 \times 10^{4} \times 1.4 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 10^{-4}}{4 \times 20 \times 10^{-3}}\)

\(= 55.24\) mV

subtopic: Generators, Back emf and Energy Transfer
stem: A rotating armature of a simple generator consists of rectangular section DABC of a conducting wire as shown in the figure, to which connections are made through sliding contacts. The armature is rotated at 1500 rpm in the magnetic field \((\vec{B})\) of 0.5 N/A.m. Determine the induced emf between the terminals P and Q of the generator at the instant shown in the adjoining figure.
solution:
The wire AB (\(l = 10\) cm) is moving to the right with the tangential velocity v.

\(\left| \vec{\mathrm{v}} \right| = \left| \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r} \right|\)

v \(= \omega r\) where \(\omega\) is angular velocity and \(r\) is the radius.

\(\mathrm{v} = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \cdot r\)  \(\left[ \because \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \right]\)

\(= 2\pi \nu r\)

\(= 2\pi \cdot \left( \dfrac{1500}{60\,\mathrm{s}} \right) \cdot \left( \dfrac{4}{100} \right) \mathrm{m}\)  \(\left[ \because r = AD = (4/100)\,\mathrm{m} \right]\)

\(= 2\pi\) m/s

\(= 6.284\) m/s

The magnetic field is directed vertically upward from North to South pole. As the wire AB is cutting the magnetic lines of force perpendicularly, the induced emf is, therefore, maximum.

\(\because e = Bl\mathrm{v} \sin\theta\) with \(\theta = 90^\circ\),

Then, \(e = e_{\max} = Bl\mathrm{v}\)

\(= (0.5\ \text{N/A.m})\,(10/100)\,\text{m} \cdot (6.28\ \text{m/s})\)

\(= \dfrac{0.5}{10} \times 6.28\)

\(= 0.314\) V

or \(e_{\max} \approx 314.2\) mV.

The emf induced in the wires BC and DA is zero because the magnetic Lorentz force on free electrons in these wire \(\left[ \vec{F} = q(\vec{\mathrm{v}} \times \vec{B}) \right]\) has no component parallel to the wires. Also there is no e.m.f. in the lead in wires, which are stationary and are not in motion \((\vec{\mathrm{v}} = 0)\). Therefore the total emf between the terminals P and Q is due the movement of segment AB. i.e., \(e = 314\) mV. The direction of induced emf is given by Lenz's law.

stem: A conducting loop of area 1 m\(^2\) is placed normal to uniform magnetic field 3 Wb/m\(^2\). If the magnetic field is uniformly reduced to 1 Wb/m\(^2\) in a time of 0.5 s, calculate the induced emf produced in the loop.
solution:
Given,

Area of the loop, \(A = 1\) m\(^2\)

\((B)_{\text{initial}} = 3\) Wb/m\(^2\)

\((B)_{\text{final}} = 1\) Wb/m\(^2\)

duration of time, \(\Delta t = 0.5\) s

\(\therefore\) Induced emf,

\(|e| = \left| \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t} \right| = \left| \dfrac{\phi_{\text{final}} - \phi_{\text{initial}}}{\text{Time interval}} \right|\)

\(= \dfrac{(B_{\text{final}} - B_{\text{initial}})A}{\Delta t}\)

\(= \left| \left[ \dfrac{(1-3)}{0.5} \cdot 1 \right] \right|\) volt

\(= \left| -\dfrac{2}{0.5} \cdot 1 \right|\) volt

\(|e| = 4\) volt
